messages:
ashley-g: Quick follow-up from the memory postmortem — compiling a focused remediation checklist so we have owners and short timelines. Posting proposed items, pls react with :thumbsup: if you own one or reply with availability.

rahul: I can take profiling + flamegraphing for slow paths. Goal: get concrete hotspots within 3 business days.

marta: I’ll own GC/compaction tuning experiments. Plan to run A/B on staging starting tomorrow.

ashley-g: Thanks. Here are the items I’m tracking: 1) continuous KV cache profiling (rahul) 2) GC/compaction tuning (marta) 3) eviction/limit policy audit (tim-c) 4) OOM guardrails + cgroup limits (leo) 5) weekly regression check (ops-bot -> alerts).

tim-c: I’ll audit eviction policies and config drift. ETA 4 days. Will push a config diff with comments.

leo: I’ll own the runaway-oom guardrails. Immediate action: add soft cgroup limits + oom_score_adj for runtime jobs. Plan to roll tomorrow morning.

rahul: Quick note on profiling approach — using async flamegraphs + jemalloc stats. Command I’ll run on a canary: ```sudo perf record -g -p $(pgrep inference_runtime) -- sleep 30; perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg```

marta: For GC, I want to test increasing compaction frequency and lowering max_live_segments. Hypothesis: reduces fragmentation but may spike CPU. Scheduling runs: staging @ 10:00 PT.

ashley-g: Logging owner+deadline matrix here. Please confirm actual due dates. If you need help, ask.

tim-c: Confirmed — I'll open PR: "kv: eviction-policy-audit-2027" and assign to @marta for review.

leo: Rolling guardrails to prod in canary mode at 06:00 UTC. Will monitor memory graphs and annotate alerts channel.

ops-bot: Automated alert rule created: "kv_cache_memory_regression" -> notify #eng-runtime + oncall after 3 spikes in 10m.

marta: After initial runs, I'll post CSV of fragmentation metrics. If compaction reduces tail latency < 5% and memory stays within 85% of limit, we keep change.

rahul: Found two hotspots in parser path and kv-iterator hold. Will attach simpler repro and small patch to reduce alloc churn.

ashley-g: Good. Two follow-ups for product: (A) if we need more headroom short-term, enable conservative eviction policy for >1h request paths; (B) longer-term redesign of iterator to avoid retained buffers.

tim-c: Noted. I’ll add the conservative eviction toggle to runtime flags: `--kv-eviction=conservative`. Will document tradeoffs.

leo: Observability checklist: add memory histogram by service + heapdump on OOM (upload to s3/inference-dumps). Will PR alert runbook.

ashley-g: Deadline roundup: rahul (profiling) — +3 days; marta (GC experiments) — +2 days for initial results; tim-c (policy audit) — +4 days; leo (guardrails) — deploy tomorrow; ops-bot (alerts) — done. If anyone needs to shift, reply here.

marta: Small ask — can infra provide a staging cluster with identical KV size distribution? Current staging is ~1/5th which may hide fragmentation.

ashley-g: @infra-team ping — can we clone a dataset snapshot for a one-off staging run?

ops-bot: infra-team auto-assignment: ticket #INF-4987 created for dataset snapshot. ETA 48 hours.

rahul: If infra can’t, I’ll generate synthetic keys to approximate distribution and post generator script.

tim-c: Also adding a dogfooding checklist so SREs can kick long-running queries under controlled load.

leo: I’ll coordinate monitoring dashboard cards: memory by host, kv-cache-resident, GC pause stats.

ashley-g: Thanks team — I’ll convert this into a follow-up doc and ping for a 15m sync if needed after initial results. For now, reactions == ownership confirmation. :rocket:
